title: Does an Eytzinger array make static key lookup faster?

claims.text: For static ordered keys in RAM, an Eytzinger (breadth-first) array layout with branch-free traversal and software prefetching can outperform an optimized sorted-array binary search for single-threaded point queries when the data exceed the last-level cache.

The same Eytzinger-plus-prefetch implementation retains a throughput advantage over optimized sorted-array binary search when multiple reader threads execute independent point queries concurrently on the same static RAM-resident key set exceeding the last-level cache.

criteria.layout: Is the tested layout a breadth-first Eytzinger array?
criteria.prefetch: Does the measured implementation use software prefetching and branch-free traversal?
criteria.baseline: Is the comparator an optimized sorted-array binary search, not merely an unoptimized baseline?
criteria.working_set: Are static keys RAM-resident and is a measured case larger than last-level cache?
criteria.measurement: Are query latency or throughput actually measured, with hardware and workload described?
criteria.concurrency: Are multiple independent reader threads tested on the shared static data structure?
